corrections.what_happened: The two non-LLM context scores compared each gold record, written as its string values joined by spaces, with the texts handed over, written in HERB's own form, so the same record did not match itself.

before.what_it_did: each gold record as all of its string values joined by spaces, against the texts as handed over (eval/ragas.py at the commits that scored the three final runs on the hundred)

rule.text:
1. The evaluation compared gold records and handed-over texts in two forms that are not the
     same. The code that scored the three final runs on the hundred wrote each gold record as all
     of its string values joined by spaces, while every arm hands its records over in HERB's own
     form (harness.record_text), with ids, labels, dates and names around the content, so the
     same record did not match itself as a string. The code that scored the runs on the 715
     answerable questions wrote each gold record in record_text form, so the ids, labels, dates
     and names of the form were counted in how alike two records are.
  2. The artefact hands over chunks of several records; a whole chunk was compared with single
     gold records and never matched one.
  3. Both sides are reduced to record content (harness.record_content): each gold record's
     content, against the content of each record handed over, every text cut into its records
     (eval.ragas.contents_handed_over).
  4. context_recall_nonllm and context_precision_nonllm are calculated again by RAGAS's own
     NonLLMContextRecall and NonLLMContextPrecisionWithReference on those contents; every other
     score and every other file stays as it is.

not_changed_and_worth_knowing: No answer, context, context_ids, other score or judge call is changed; arm_outputs.jsonl is as it was. The content is taken out only for these two scores; the answer model and the judge got the texts as they were handed over.
Content against content still counts different records as alike when their text is more than half the same, as HERB's templated Slack messages often are (output/research/2026-10-23-nonllm-checks).

corrections.what_happened: 1 scoring starts wrote no entry in judge_legs: their processes were killed or their machine shut down before the start ended. Their judge calls and embedder requests are in eval_calls.jsonl and their cells in eval_results.jsonl, so judge_usage, the sum of the entries, was short of them. 2 written entries named no start (prod/run.py --rejudge writes its entries with no settings) and now name the start they belong to.

rule.text:
1. A scoring start is missing when eval_calls.jsonl holds records with its eval_leg and no entry
     of judge_legs has that time as its settings.started_at. An entry that names no start (a start
     of prod/run.py --rejudge writes its entry with no settings) belongs to the one start, not named
     by another entry, whose judge calls that answered, counted by rule 2, are the entry's calls and
     whose last call record ended before the entry's timestamp; it gets that start as
     settings.started_at. When no start, or more than one, fits an entry, nothing is written.
  2. Its usage is counted from its records the way the harness counts a judge call (eval.ragas,
     harness.chat): calls = its judge call records that answered (ok); attempts = their tries;
     tokens_in, cached_input_tokens and tokens_out = the sums of those calls' usage; request_s =
     the seconds of each call's try that answered; retry_s = the seconds of its other tries and of
     every pause between tries; time_s = from each call's started_at to its finished_at;
     reasoning_tokens and wait_s 0, as the harness always has them. A judge call that gave up (no
     try answered) counts in none of these, as in the harness.
  3. Its judge_model is the one model of its judge calls (empty when it made none); its
     judge_backend the evaluation's. Its settings hold started_at (its eval_leg), interrupted (that
     the start wrote no entry) and embedding (its embedder records summed: requests, texts,
     tokens_in, lock_wait_s, encode_s, as the harness sums them). Its timestamp, elapsed_s and
     settings.finished_at are empty: when the start ended is not recorded. Nothing else of the
     settings is recorded for it.
  4. The entries stand in the order of their starts. judge_usage is their sum, as the harness sums
     it; judge_elapsed_s stays the sum of the entries' elapsed_s. No written entry changes but for
     the settings.started_at of rule 1; no score, cell or call record changes.
  5. The same counting is done on every written entry's start and compared with that entry; what
     differs is printed and kept with the correction, and changes nothing.

not_changed_and_worth_knowing: A cell under way when a start's process ended wrote no call record; what its calls cost is in no file and in no rebuilt entry.
When a rebuilt start ended is not recorded; each change gives the end of its last call record.
judge_elapsed_s stays the sum of the written entries' elapsed_s.
No written entry, score, cell or call record is changed.

settings.interrupted: the start wrote no entry; rebuilt from its records in eval_calls.jsonl by correction missing-judge-legs/2 (corrections.json)

checks.what: rule 5: each written entry's counts (calls, attempts, tokens in, cached and out) are those of its start's records, counted by rule 2

judge_usage less the score cells' usage is the judge calls that answered in cells with no row in eval_results.jsonl (cells that failed, or that a later start dropped)
